items.title: 2.2 Effect of an electric field on the fundamental particles

source_refs.note: Topic 2.2, printed pages 24-25: the behaviour of the three particles in an electric field (Figure 2.1).

blocks.text: The behaviour of particles in an electric field depends on their mass and charge. If beams of electrons, protons and neutrons pass one by one at the same speed through an electric field, they behave as follows.

items: Neutrons, being neutral, are not deflected; they travel in a straight path perpendicular to the direction of the field.
Protons, being positively charged, are deflected towards the negative plate.
Electrons, being negatively charged, are deflected towards the positive plate, and to a much greater extent, since they are 1/1836 as heavy as protons.

blocks.alt: A beam of particles leaves a slit on the left and passes between two charged plates, the negative plate above and the positive plate below. The proton path p+ bends slightly up towards the negative plate, the neutron path n goes straight, and the electron path e- bends more strongly down towards the positive plate; the angle of deflection theta is marked between the n and e- paths.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.1: Behaviour of proton, electron and neutron in the electric field (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 2.1).

blocks.text: The amount of deviation from the original direction is measured in two ways: the angle of deflection is proportional to charge over mass, and the radius of deflection is proportional to mass over charge. The radius is defined by imagining that after deflection the particle moves in a circular path, so the factors affecting the radius are the reciprocal of those for the angle.
